respuesta.pregunta: In payment-promise-gateway 0.0.10-test-crc-migration, when I call GET /forgiveness_proposal/{promiseId}, what does the service call downstream, and how does it get the forgiveness data it returns?
respuesta.respuesta:
When the request comes in, the PaymentPromiseController first checks the format of promiseId, which is a numeric path parameter. It then calls getLateFeeForgiveness(promiseId) on PaymentPromiseService [payment-promise-gateway/0.0.10-test-crc-migration/guide/README.md:L258-L261]. Next, the service calls getPaymentPromiseById(promiseId) on PromiseService and gets back a PaymentPromiseDTO [payment-promise-gateway/0.0.10-test-crc-migration/guide/README.md:L262-L263].

The service has no separate call for forgiveness data. It takes the lateFeeForgiveness out of that PaymentPromiseDTO itself and returns a LateFeeForgivenessDTO to the controller. The controller then sends the forgiveness details back to the user as JSON [payment-promise-gateway/0.0.10-test-crc-migration/guide/README.md:L264-L266].
answer_checks: Indicates that the service calls getPaymentPromiseById(promiseId) on PromiseService and receives a PaymentPromiseDTO.
Explains that the service extracts lateFeeForgiveness from the PaymentPromiseDTO and returns a LateFeeForgivenessDTO.
Mentions that the controller validates the promiseId format (numeric) before calling the service's getLateFeeForgiveness.
Cites the sequence diagram for GET /forgiveness_proposal/{promiseId} in the 0.0.10-test-crc-migration README.
Does not invent additional downstream calls or fields not shown in the diagram.
